note: TWO checkpoints in one container, unlike every other model here: the landmark network consumes a cropped and rotated palm ROI and cannot find a hand in a frame by itself, so shipping only it would produce a model that answers 'no hand here' to every image. The FLOAT variants are taken deliberately, not because float is the default: the int8 files in the same repos are unusable. Measured on the test frame -- palm int8 peaks at 0.0216 score where float reaches 0.8939 (and cv2.dnn aborts inside its int8 pool layer outright), and landmark int8 puts the wrist 35 px off (197.7 vs 232.5). On this host ORT's int8 kernels are also slower than float: 11.62 ms vs 5.18 ms for palm, 4.45 ms vs 0.94 ms for landmark. The palm detector's 2016 SSD anchors are NOT shipped: they are generated by tools/pack/packers/hands.py as cell centres -- 576 cells of a 24x24 grid at 2 anchors each, then 144 cells of a 12x12 grid at 6 each, 1152+864=2016 -- which reproduces the OpenCV zoo's literal table to 7.5e-9. That residue is the zoo's own 8-decimal truncation, not a different formula; it is 4e-7 px on a 520-pixel frame.
